concepts.name: Restoring state needed to interpret an activity result

questions.prompt: An Android activity registers a camera result callback only inside the camera button's click listener. What change supports delivery after process recreation?

choices.text: Register the callback unconditionally on every activity creation
Register the callback only when the saved-state bundle is null
Register a new callback inside each returned-result callback
Register the callback only when the camera activity is already running

questions.explanation: The callback must exist after recreation even when no new click occurs. Registration is unconditional; launching can remain conditional. Waiting for a running camera, registering on result or skipping restored creations misses that requirement.

sources.title: Get a result from an activity
sources.claim: Activity-result callbacks must register unconditionally in the same order on each recreation; registration occurs before creation, launching waits until CREATED, and extra state needed for processing results must be saved separately.

questions.prompt: A ComponentActivity stores the launcher returned by `registerForActivityResult()` in a member initializer. When may it call that launcher's `launch()`?

choices.text: Only after the activity lifecycle reaches `STARTED`
Only after the activity lifecycle reaches `RESUMED`
After the activity lifecycle reaches `CREATED`
Immediately in the initializer before the activity is created

questions.explanation: Registration can precede activity creation, but launching must wait until CREATED. The APIs separate registering a callback from launching. STARTED and RESUMED are later lifecycle states, not the minimum required by the launcher; invoking it before creation is too early.

questions.prompt: An Android app launches an editor for a selected database row and stores the row ID only in an activity field. The process dies before the editor returns. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Re-registering the result callback recreates arbitrary activity fields
The callback must be available in the recreated activity
State needed to interpret the result must be saved separately
The original activity field is guaranteed to survive process death
The Activity Result APIs automatically persist the selected row object

questions.explanation: Activity Result APIs support callback delivery after recreation, but additional application state needs its own saved/restored mechanism. Unconditionally re-register the callback and restore the row ID. Arbitrary fields and selected objects are not automatically persisted and the original activity instance is gone.

questions.prompt: An Android activity registers two result launchers, but reverses their registration order after recreation. What is the risk?

choices.text: The framework automatically sorts registration by callback names
An in-flight result may be routed to the wrong callback
Registration order matters only when both launchers run simultaneously
Both launchers become safe because contracts determine every routing key

questions.explanation: The documentation requires the same registration order on each creation to route in-flight results correctly. Contract types and callback names do not replace that ordering requirement, even if only one request is in flight.

questions.prompt: What does calling Android's `registerForActivityResult()` do by itself?

choices.text: Invokes the callback immediately with the last persisted result
Starts the external activity immediately using the contract defaults
Registers the callback and returns a launcher for a later request
Advances the activity lifecycle so the external request can launch

questions.explanation: Registration sets up handling and returns an ActivityResultLauncher. Calling launch starts a request; registration does not itself start an external activity, force a callback or advance lifecycle state.

questions.prompt: An Android activity-result callback needs a draft ID after process recreation. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The original activity instance field remains available after process death
Register the result callback on the recreated activity too
Save and restore the draft ID separately from launcher registration
The launcher automatically persists every local variable captured by a callback
The result contract reconstructs arbitrary application draft selections

questions.explanation: Additional state needs a separate save/restore mechanism, and the callback must be registered on recreation. Registration does not persist arbitrary closures or application selection; the original activity instance cannot survive process death.
